candidates.title: From Lethargy to Recovery: Central Diabetes Insipidus from Pituitary Metastasis in Recurrent HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treated with Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki.
candidates.abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer is well known for its aggressive nature and high incidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastasis, often affecting the brain parenchyma or leptomeninges. However, metastasis to the pituitary gland is exceedingly rare. We report a case of ER/PR-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer recurrence presenting with panhypopituitarism (PH) and central diabetes insipidus (CDI), resulting in hypernatremia-induced altered mental status. The patient had completed prior treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, lumpectomy, and trastuzumab. Imaging revealed a temporal lobe mass with suprasellar enhancement. Surgical resection confirmed breast carcinoma metastasis. Hormonal studies confirmed PH and CDI. Management involved DDAVP, corticosteroids, fluid correction, whole-brain radiation, and systemic therapy with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (ENHERTU), leading to significant neurological recovery. This case highlights a rare metastatic pattern and the need for high clinical suspicion and multidisciplinary intervention.

candidates.title: Ruxolitinib improves outcomes in association with altered fibroblast immunobiology in mouse models of Sjögren's disease.
candidates.abstract: Sjögren Disease (SjD) is a common rheumatologic disease with symptoms of dryness attributed to autoimmune exocrinopathy. JAK-STAT signaling pathway activity contributes to SjD salivary gland pathogenesis. We hypothesized that treatment of SjD model mice with ruxolitinib, a JAK-inhibitor, would improve disease course. NOD.B10 and Aec SjD model mice were treated with vehicle or ruxolitinib for two weeks. We measured plasma immunoglobulins and cytokines, and assessed submandibular salivary glands (SMSGs) histologically, with flow cytometry, and spatial transcriptomics. Aec mice had a more robust inflammatory profile than NOD.B10 mice as measured by SMSG lymphocytic infiltrate, peripheral immunoglobulins and cytokine concentrations. Ruxolitinib treatment reduced plasma [IgG], [CXCL13], and focus score in Aec but not NOD.B10 mice. In Aec mice, flow cytometry showed reductions in phosphorylated (p) STAT1 in SMSG epithelial cells, leukocytes, and fibroblasts with treatment. pSTAT1 correlated with salivary flow rate and focus score. Spatial transcriptomic sequencing and immunofluorescence of SMSGs revealed a treatment effect upon fibroblast-macrophage spatial relationships. Ruxolitinib treatment improved disease course in Aec mice but not NOD.B10 mice, suggesting these mice model different SjD subpopulations and ruxolitinib efficacy may be subpopulation dependent. Flow cytometry, spatial transcriptomics, and immunostaining results implicated ruxolitinib-induced changes of fibroblast-immune cell interactions in the SMSG thereby suggesting these unique interactions as a pathogenic element and novel treatment target. These results underscore the therapeutic potential of JAK-STAT pathway inhibition for treatment of SjD, and with ruxolitinib specifically, at least for specific SjD subpopulations.

candidates.title: Comparative effectiveness of infliximab and tofacitinib in advanced therapy-naive and -exposed patients with ulcerative colitis: a multicenter real-world study.
candidates.abstract: and Aim: Infliximab (IFX) and tofacitinib (TOF) are advanced therapies for ulcerative colitis (UC), but real-world comparative data by prior advanced therapy (AT) exposure remain limited. We compared effectiveness by prior AT exposure. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with UC who initiated IFX or TOF between June 2010 and May 2025. The primary analysis was restricted to May 2018 onward, when both were available in Japan. AT-naive and AT-exposed cohorts were analyzed separately using overlap weighting. The primary outcome was corticosteroid-free clinical remission at week 52. Of 266 patients (137 IFX, 129 TOF), the primary analysis included 76 AT-naive (27 IFX, 49 TOF) and 120 AT-exposed (40 IFX, 80 TOF) patients. Week 14 remission did not differ significantly between treatments in either cohort. At week 52, remission numerically favored TOF in AT-naive patients (IFX, 43.9%; TOF, 64.5%; odds ratio [OR], 2.32; 95% CI, 0.84-6.44; P = .105), whereas remission was higher with TOF in the AT-exposed cohort (IFX, 19.0%; TOF, 38.8%; OR, 2.71; 95% CI, 1.08-6.80; nominal P = .034). Three-year treatment persistence did not differ significantly in either cohort but numerically favored TOF in AT-naive patients (IFX, 39.2%; TOF, 61.5%; hazard ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.31-1.36). Multiple-imputation analyses yielded similar findings. Week 52 remission numerically favored TOF in AT-naive patients and was higher with TOF in AT-exposed patients. Clinically relevant differences in 3-year persistence could not be ruled out, particularly in AT-naive patients. These findings are exploratory.

candidates.title: Epstein-Barr virus and inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review of its clinical significance and potential pathogenic role.
candidates.abstract: Several studies report an association between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This review critically synthesizes current evidence on these association between EBV and IBD, its potential mechanisms, clinical implications, and research gaps. A systematic search identified studies investigating EBV in IBD using serological, molecular, and tissue-based approaches. Data on EBV prevalence, viral load, disease phenotype, treatment status, and clinical outcomes were extracted, and study quality was assessed. A narrative review examined proposed mechanisms that may potentially link EBV to intestinal inflammation. From 7271 citations, 45 studies met inclusion criteria. EBV was more frequently detected in intestinal tissue from IBD patients than in controls, particularly in active or refractory disease, whereas findings for seroprevalence and blood-based markers were less consistent. Some longitudinal studies reported associations between prior EBV exposure and subsequent IBD, particularly Crohn's disease, but these observations do not establish a causal relationship. Proposed mechanisms involving EBV-infected B cells, molecular mimicry, and altered cytokine signaling provide biological plausibility but remain unproven in IBD. EBV latency programs and age at seroconversion may influence disease progression and reactivation risk, although data remain limited. Corticosteroids and therapy with infliximab plus azathioprine have been associated with higher EBV loads, especially in refractory disease, yet these findings may be confounded by disease severity and treatment exposure. Current evidence supports an association between EBV and IBD, particularly in severe and refractory disease but does not establish-and equally does not exclude-a pathogenic role for EBV. Considerable methodological heterogeneity in study design and EBV detection methods and the observational nature of the available data limit causal interpretation. Prospective mechanistic studies are needed to determine whether EBV is a causal contributor, a disease modifier, or a marker of underlying immune dysregulation.

candidates.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome in Adulthood: Diagnostic Recognition, Clinical Spectrum, and Long-Term Follow-Up.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome is usually diagnosed during childhood, and data on outcomes in adulthood are limited. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated the diagnostic history, endocrine phenotype, and clinical outcomes of 14 adults with radiologically confirmed pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. The cohort comprised eight men and six women, with a mean age of 28.8±6.4 years and a mean documented follow-up at our center of 5.6±3.2 years. Hypopituitarism was diagnosed during childhood in 12 patients and during adulthood in 2 patients. Thirteen patients had deficiencies of all four anterior pituitary hormone axes, whereas one patient had growth hormone and gonadotropic deficiencies with preserved corticotropic and thyrotropic functions. In six patients diagnosed during childhood, pituitary stalk interruption syndrome was recognized only after later reassessment of pituitary imaging. Eleven patients received growth hormone treatment during childhood, and 13 of 14 patients reached their calculated target height. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia were each present in 10 patients. Four patients had bone mineral density below the expected range for age. One female patient achieved a live birth following in vitro fertilization. In this real-world cohort, the skeletal and metabolic findings observed despite generally favorable growth outcomes support the need for lifelong endocrine follow-up.
candidates.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme

candidates.title: A Diagnostic Conundrum: A Hemorrhagic Adrenal Mass With Discordant Radiological, Biochemical, and Pathologic Features.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas vary in their identity, making accurate diagnosis essential for management. Interpretation of these lesions using radiology, biochemistry, or pathology can be confounded by hemorrhagic changes, medication effects, and limitations of imaging. To prevent misclassification, an integrated assessment is crucial. We present a case of a 71-year-old male with an incidentally discovered left adrenal mass that exhibited computed tomography and MRI imaging findings concerning for pheochromocytoma or adrenal malignancy. Biochemical analysis ruled out pheochromocytoma and was suggestive of possible glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid co-secretion, although clinical urgency of surgical resection precluded completion of confirmatory endocrinologic testing. The lesion was initially diagnosed as a benign endothelial adrenal cyst on pathologic review. Because of the discordance among the radiological, biochemical, and initial pathologic findings, an integrated histologic re-evaluation was requested. The mass was ultimately reclassified as an adrenocortical adenoma with extensive hemorrhagic and cystic changes. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary integration when evaluating adrenal lesions with confounding features and underscores how suggestive (though incomplete) biochemical evidence can appropriately drive pathological re-evaluation.

candidates.title: Levamisole-Induced Cutaneous Vasculitis/Vasculopathy: A Concise Review.
candidates.abstract: Levamisole-induced cutaneous vasculitis represents a distinctive form of drug-induced vasculopathy that has emerged as a significant clinical challenge, particularly since the widespread use of levamisole as a cocaine adulterant. This review provides a concise overview of this entity, with a specific focus on its epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, histopathological features, immunological profile, and therapeutic management. Key clinical features include stellate or retiform purpura with a predilection for the ears and extremities, characteristic serological findings with mixed antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody positivity, and distinctive histopathological patterns showing both leukocytoclastic vasculitis and thrombotic vasculopathy. Recognition of this entity is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management, as its treatment differs substantially from that of primary antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitides. This review synthesizes current evidence to provide clinicians and pathologists with a practical overview of this increasingly recognized condition.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of Psychological Interventions for Smoking Cessation Targeting Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review.
candidates.abstract: Tobacco cessation is a public health priority. However, long-term outcomes remain limited, partly due to insufficient adaptation of interventions to chronic conditions, such as diabetes mellitus (DM), a leading cause of chronic disability worldwide. Evidence regarding the clinical impact of smoking cessation treatments in people with DM remains inconsistent. The objective of this study was to examine the effectiveness of psychological smoking cessation interventions for individuals with type 1 and type 2 DM. A search for scientific studies was conducted in four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, SCOPUS, and PsycINFO), resulting in the selection of 12 studies following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO, ID: CRD42024531545). Overall, 83.3% of the interventions incorporated diabetes-adapted components. Programs frequently achieved short-term reductions in cigarette consumption, although complete long-term abstinence was less frequent. Only a minority of studies demonstrated statistically significant higher abstinence rates in the intervention groups than in the control groups, ranging from 31.3% to 70.6% at 6 months and 20.0% to 38.8% at 12 months. The most favorable outcomes occurred in group-based, multicomponent programs for type 2 DM combining diabetes-specific psychoeducation, motivational strategies, and optional pharmacotherapy. Due to a moderate-to-high risk of bias across studies, evidence regarding the effectiveness of psychological smoking cessation interventions for individuals with DM remains limited. Further research is needed to identify factors that influence smoking cessation outcomes in patients with DM. The integration of evidence-based programs and interventions tailored to diabetes-related needs, associated comorbidities, and gender-specific factors are essential to address these challenges.
candidates.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Safety, recovery, and hospital resource use after robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection in a 48-hour short-stay pathway: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract: To compare perioperative safety, early recovery, and resource use between a short-stay pathway and conventional inpatient care for robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection. This single-center retrospective cohort included 110 patients who underwent robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection: 47 managed in a short-stay pathway with discharge planned within 48 h of hospital admission and 63 managed with conventional inpatient care during the same period. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications, unplanned intensive care, emergency attendance, readmission, reoperation, or death. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic instability, postoperative hypotension and hypoglycemia, pain, opioid consumption, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), length of stay, costs, pathway completion, and patient satisfaction. Welch t tests and Fisher exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons, and absolute risk differences (RDs) and mean differences are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Exploratory linear models with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, ASA class, tumor size, and duration of alpha blockade; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for surgeon, surgical approach, secretory phenotype, and hypertension. Baseline, comorbidity, endocrine, and operative characteristics were similar between groups (all standardized mean differences < 0.30). The 30-day composite safety outcome occurred in 1 of 47 short-stay patients (2.1%) and 1 of 63 conventional inpatients (1.6%; RD 0.5% points, 95% CI -6.6 to 9.6; P = 1.000). Intraoperative hemodynamic instability was also similar (83.0% vs. 87.3%; P = 0.590), as were persistent postoperative hypotension (8.5% vs. 7.9%) and postoperative hypoglycemia (8.5% vs. 7.9%). The planned 48-hour discharge target was achieved in 44 of 47 patients (93.6%). Compared with conventional care, the short-stay pathway had lower 24-hour pain scores (mean 1.8 vs. 2.4), total inpatient opioid exposure (8.7 vs. 17.7 mg morphine milligram equivalents), postoperative stay (44.2 vs. 105.1 h), total stay (49.2 vs. 476.4 h), and total in-hospital cost (CNY 49,858 vs. CNY 64,802), with higher 24-hour QoR-15 (119.7 vs. 107.9) and satisfaction (9.2 vs. 8.2); these differences remained significant after Holm correction and were consistent in fully adjusted sensitivity analyses. Among selected patients undergoing robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection, the short-stay pathway was associated with similar observed perioperative safety outcomes, faster recovery, shorter hospitalization, lower in-hospital costs, and higher patient satisfaction than conventional inpatient care. Because only two composite events occurred and the 95% CI of the risk difference was wide, these findings provide preliminary evidence of feasibility rather than proof of equivalent safety, and support prospective validation.

candidates.title: Solitary Neurofibroma in the Submental Region of a 15-Year-Old Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
candidates.abstract: Neurofibroma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and fibroblasts. It may occur sporadically or as part of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Solitary neurofibroma arising in the submental region of an adolescent is extremely rare. We report a case of a solitary submental neurofibroma in a 15-year-old male and highlight its diagnostic and management implications. A 15-year-old adolescent boy presented with a chronic, painless right submental swelling that had been present for one year and had enlarged over the preceding three months. Clinical examination revealed a rubbery, nontender, approximately 3×3×4 cm mass without skin changes or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history suggestive of NF1, neural tumors, or pheochromocytoma. Ultrasound and CT imaging showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass consistent with a benign neurogenic tumor. The mass was completely excised via a submental incision. Histopathological examination confirmed a solitary neurofibroma with Schwann cell and fibroblast proliferation within a collagen matrix, Antoni A and B patterns, and positive S-100 immunostaining, with no evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and tongue and floor-of-mouth function were preserved. Solitary submental neurofibroma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of submental masses in adolescents, even in the absence of NF1 features. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice and allows definitive histopathological diagnosis. A thorough evaluation for NF1 is recommended to guide long-term management and follow-up.

candidates.title: A Review of Platelet-Rich Plasma as Treatment for Partial Elbow Ulnar Collateral Ligament Tears.
candidates.abstract: Platelet-rich plasma injections are increasingly utilized for partial-thickness ulnar collateral ligament tears in throwing athletes. This narrative review evaluates platelet-rich plasma's efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness for partial ulnar collateral ligament tears using literature from 2020 to 2026. A systematic search identified four studies, including cohorts and an economic simulation model. The largest cohort demonstrated that 60% of athletes with partial tears returned to play when platelet-rich plasma was combined with rehabilitation. Smaller case series reported successful return to play with similar treatment, though limited by a lack of comparison groups and small sample sizes. Complications included ulnar nerve dysfunction, particularly in athletes with preexisting nerve instability. Early surgery was often more cost-effective for long-term career durability. Current evidence suggests platelet-rich plasma alongside rehabilitation may benefit select athletes with partial ulnar collateral ligament injuries but is limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous protocols, and inconsistent outcome measures. Future research is needed regarding patient selection and standardized treatment protocols.

candidates.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.

candidates.title: Durable Complete Response to Pembrolizumab for Postoperative Nodal Recurrence of Lynch Syndrome-Associated Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes cause Lynch syndrome and are associated with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) may respond favorably to immune checkpoint inhibitors. A 54-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome and a germline MSH2 mutation developed right renal pelvic carcinoma. The tumor was diagnosed as a pT3 high-grade urothelial carcinoma, and the patient underwent laparoscopic nephroureterectomy. She was subsequently administered adjuvant gemcitabine and carboplatin due to a contraindication for cisplatin. Due to nodal recurrence, pembrolizumab was initiated at 200 mg every 3 weeks, achieving a complete radiological and metabolic response after five cycles. The course was complicated by immune-related adrenal insufficiency, which was managed with corticosteroid replacement therapy. Pembrolizumab may achieve a durable complete response in Lynch syndrome-associated UTUC. MSI screening should be considered in UTUC to guide decision-making.

candidates.title: MACS: mild by definition, challenging by nature.
candidates.abstract: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is the most frequent form of cortisol excess in patients with adrenal incidentalomas. Although it lacks the classical phenotype of overt Cushing's syndrome, MACS is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant condition associated with multisystem complications rather than a benign biochemical finding. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic limitations, and management of MACS, with particular focus on cardiometabolic, skeletal, muscular, neuropsychiatric, frailty-related, reproductive, and emerging microbiome-related consequences. Chronic exposure to low-grade cortisol excess is being recognized as a factor associated with hypertension, disorders of glucose metabolism, dyslipidemia, increased cardiovascular risk, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, skeletal fragility, impaired muscle function, frailty, sleep and circadian disturbances, cognitive and mood alterations, hypogonadism, and possible changes in gut microbiota. The 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, but its interpretation is limited by assay variability, medication interference, comorbidities, and imperfect reflection of long-term tissue glucocorticoid exposure. Emerging approaches, including steroid profiling, hair cortisol/cortisone, salivary cortisone, inflammatory indices, metabolomic tools, and exploratory biomarkers related to microbial metabolites, may improve risk stratification in the future but remain investigational. Management should be individualized. Adrenalectomy may benefit selected patients with unilateral disease and clinically relevant cortisol-related comorbidities, whereas evidence supporting pharmacological therapy remains limited. MACS should be regarded as a heterogeneous multisystem condition requiring structured clinical assessment and individualized management. Prospective studies are needed to define clinically meaningful endpoints, refine diagnostic thresholds, and identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention.

candidates.title: Low sensitivity of the pulse-controlled ergometry test as diagnostic tool for cholinergic urticaria.
candidates.abstract: Background. Cholinergic urticaria (CholU) is characterized by itchy wheals induced by physical exercise, yet validated tools for diagnosis and severity assessment remain limited. The Pulse-Controlled Ergometry (PCE) test and Cholinergic Urticaria Severity Index (CholUSI) were only evaluated in a limited number of patients. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic value of the PCE test and CholUSI for monitoring CholU severity in an unselected CholU population. Methods. Retrospective study including all patients with a clinical diagnosis of CholU, based on exercise-induced wheals and pruritus by history and/or photo-documentation, between 2021 and 2024. Patient characteristics, urticaria control test (UCT), response to omalizumab, and outcome of CholUSI and PCE test (performed before initiation of additional treatment) were investigated. Results. Thirty-nine CholU patients (66.7% male, median age 25.0 years, mean UCT 2.0) were included. CholUSI showed a strong and statistically significant correlation with UCT (p = -0.895; p < 0.01) at baseline and follow-up. CholUSI improved significantly from baseline to end of treatment in patients treated with omalizumab (n=20) (CholUSI 17.5 vs 4.0, p < 0.01; UCT 2 vs 15.5, p < 0.01). The PCE test had a sensitivity of only 62.5% (n = 10/16, 95% CI 0.4-0.8). A positive PCE-test was associated with earlier sweating (5 vs 20 minutes, p = 0.03) and higher disease severity by CholUSI (18.0 vs 14.5, p < 0.01).  Conclusions. Our findings support the use of CholUSI as a practical and disease-specific tool for assessment of CholU severity and treatment response. However, the sensitivity of the PCE test was low, highlighting the need for improvement and further validation.
candidates.journal: European annals of allergy and clinical immunology

candidates.title: Incidental and ignored: Factors influencing follow-up of adrenal incidentalomas in the emergency setting.
candidates.abstract: Guidelines recommend biochemical and imaging evaluation for adrenal incidentalomas >1 cm. These lesions are often discovered during unrelated acute events and frequently overlooked. We evaluated the incidence and guideline-concordant management of adrenal incidentalomas at a quaternary referral institution. CT reports from 2016 to 2023 were screened with natural language processing to identify adrenal nodules >1 cm. Cases were retrospectively reviewed for patient characteristics, follow-up evaluation, and surgical intervention. Multivariable analysis assessed factors associated with guideline-concordant management. Among 1301 patients with adrenal lesions, only 268 patients (20.5%) underwent any biochemical evaluation. Patients with lesions noted on ER scans (n = 502) were less likely to receive biochemical workup than those in other settings (16.7% vs 23%, p = 0.027). Patients with an established PCP or hypertension were more likely to undergo follow-up, though rarely complete. Adrenal incidentaloma management infrequently adheres to guidelines, particularly when initiated in the ER, highlighting opportunities for improvement and protocolization.

candidates.title: Non-diabetic endocrine neuropathies: A practical approach to diagnosis and clinical evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy has diverse etiologies, with endocrine disorders beyond diabetes representing significant, yet frequently underrecognized causes. While diabetic neuropathy is well established, this article specifically excludes a detailed discussion of diabetic neuropathy to focus on less-recognized endocrine causes and presents a practical diagnostic algorithm for their earlier and more accurate identification. A focused narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect (2015-2025). From 2,318 screened records, 154 studies were included after full-text review of 298 articles. Evidence was synthesized by etiology, mechanism, clinical presentation and diagnostic relevance. Disorders such as hypothyroidism, acromegaly, adrenal dysfunction and deficiencies of vitamins B12 and D produce distinct neuropathic profiles via metabolic, hormonal, inflammatory or compressive mechanisms. Subclinical nerve involvement is common, with electrophysiological abnormalities detectable in up to 60% of asymptomatic individuals. Characteristic clinical patterns - such as delayed reflexes in hypothyroidism, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) in acromegaly and sensory ataxia in B12 deficiency - provide diagnostic clues. Based on synthesized evidence, a stepwise diagnostic algorithm was developed to guide clinical evaluation. Endocrine disorders are important and often reversible causes of peripheral neuropathy. Early recognition requires a systematic approach. The proposed evidence-based algorithm offers clinicians a practical tool to improve diagnostic efficiency, facilitate timely treatment of the underlying endocrine condition and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve damage.

candidates.title: Single-session radiosurgery for Cushing disease after failed resection: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
candidates.abstract: Cushing disease (CD) from an adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma causes substantial morbidity when hypercortisolism persists or recurs after transsphenoidal surgery (TSS). To define endocrine control, radiographic response, toxicity, and predictors after single-session Gamma Knife radiosurgery for residual or recurrent CD. Retrospective single-center cohort study, 1990-2026; median endocrine follow-up 54 months. Single academic tertiary referral center. 186 adults with residual or recurrent CD after ≥1 TSS and ≥12 months of follow-up. Median age 40.8 years; 78.0% female. Single-session frame-based SRS (median prescription dose 23.0 Gy; maximum dose 48.0 Gy). Prespecified primary outcome was durable biochemical control off medications (sustained 24-hour urinary free cortisol [UFC] normalization without cortisol-lowering therapy), modeled with competing-risks methodology. UFC normalized in 152 patients (81.7%), including 134 (72.0%) off all medications. Cumulative incidence of durable off-medication control was 51% (95% CI: 44-58%) at 12 months and 64% (95% CI: 56-71%) at 120 months. New endocrinopathy reached 42% (95% CI: 32-52%) at 120 months; new visual deficit occurred in 3.2%. A TSS-to-SRS interval <6 months independently predicted higher durable control (P < .001), while higher baseline AM cortisol (P < .001), whole-sella treatment (P = .013), and female gender (P = .027) predicted lower durable control. Higher maximum dose was the sole independent predictor of new endocrinopathy (P = .009). Single-session SRS achieves durable medication-free control in approximately two-thirds of patients with residual or recurrent CD, with excellent tumor control and meaningful delayed endocrine toxicity warranting long-term surveillance.
candidates.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

candidates.title: When genetics disrupt the gut: Dysmotility and ganglioneuromatosis in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B syndrome.
candidates.abstract: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B) is a rare hereditary cancer syndrome characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, and pheochromocytoma. Gastrointestinal involvement is common and often manifests as diffuse intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (IGN), which can impair motility and lead to severe constipation, pseudo-obstruction, or megacolon. We report a male infant with known MEN2B who developed progressive abdominal distension and obstructive symptoms refractory to medical management. Initial rectal suction biopsies were unrevealing. Due to persistent symptoms, a diverting ileostomy was created for decompression, during which full-thickness biopsies were obtained, ultimately establishing the definitive diagnosis of colonic ganglioneuromatosis. This case highlights the limitations of mucosal biopsies in detecting deeper neural pathology and underscores the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion for IGN in patients with MEN2B and persistent gastrointestinal symptoms despite a normal initial evaluation.

candidates.title: Outcomes from a Pilot Trial of a Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) Tobacco Cessation Intervention for Veterans at Heightened Risk for Suicide.
candidates.abstract: Tobacco use has consistently been linked to suicide risk, and some data suggest that tobacco cessation may reduce risk. However, higher risk individuals are typically excluded from clinical trials. Dialectical Behavior Therapy is a psychotherapy approach originally designed to reduce suicide risk that may also be beneficial in treating addiction by enhancing emotion regulation and distress tolerance skills. The present study was a randomized pilot trial comparing a standard tobacco cessation intervention to a DBT-based integrated intervention for tobacco cessation and suicide prevention. Veterans (n = 68) who were daily users of cigarettes and/or e-cigarettes were randomized to DBT for cessation (DBT-C) or to treatment as usual (TAU). Participants in both conditions attended 12 weekly group psychotherapy sessions and were followed for a total of 24 weeks to evaluate changes in tobacco use, suicidality, emotion regulation and overall satisfaction with the intervention. DBT-C and TAU participants did not differ in terms of abstinence at end-of-treatment or 24-week follow-up. There was a trend toward greater improvement in emotion regulation in DBT-C versus TAU. Participants generally were satisfied with the intervention. This pilot trial provides preliminary evidence that individuals who use tobacco and are at elevated suicide risk can be effectively engaged in tobacco cessation interventions, and that such interventions may benefit emotional functioning as well as reducing tobacco use. DBT-C appears to be a potentially effective approach but additional, larger-scale research is needed to enable a more thorough assessment.
candidates.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.
